alert.title: edge-ingress: 3 of 8 nodes failing LB health checks

lines.text: cni0: port 7(veth3a91f0c2) entered forwarding state
TCP: request_sock_TCP: Possible SYN flooding on port 0.0.0.0:443. Sending cookies.
nf_conntrack: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
net_ratelimit: 2417 callbacks suppressed
IPVS: rr: TCP 10.96.0.10:53 - no destination available
Readiness probe failed: Get "http://10.244.7.31:10254/healthz": context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)

question: Which line explains the connect timeouts?

explanation.cause: Conntrack table full on ingress nodes; the kernel is dropping new flows
explanation.why: A traffic surge filled nf_conntrack up to nf_conntrack_max. With no free entries the kernel can’t track new flows, so their SYNs are silently discarded — clients and LB health checks see connect timeouts, not resets. SYN cookies only relieve the listen backlog; they don’t bypass conntrack.
explanation.tell: “table full, dropping packet” is the only line saying packets are actually discarded. The SYN-flood notice says cookies are being sent — connections are still answered.

lines.text: fx cache refresh: 1284 pairs loaded in 2.31s
rates client: retrying attempt=2 err="Get \"http://rates-api.internal:8080/v1/fx?base=EUR\": context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)"
sync batch 88412 aborted: rates unavailable after 3 attempts
rates client: Get "http://rates-api.internal:8080/v1/fx?base=GBP": dial tcp 10.40.2.15:8080: connect: cannot assign requested address
circuit breaker rates-api: state=open failures=52/100 window=10s
pq: canceling statement due to user request
sync lag 412s exceeds 300s threshold

question: Which line points at the root cause?

explanation.cause: Ephemeral ports exhausted by TIME_WAIT churn to a single rates-api VIP
explanation.why: v4.18.0 stopped reusing connections, so ledger-sync opens and closes one per call. Each active close parks the 4-tuple in TIME_WAIT for 60s; at ~470 calls/s to one ip:port that’s ~28k — the whole 32768–60999 range. connect() then fails locally with EADDRNOTAVAIL before a packet leaves.
explanation.tell: “connect: cannot assign requested address” is a local error: no free source port. TIME_WAIT flatlines at ~28.2k, exactly the size of the port range, while rates-api sees no errors.

source.title: How to stop running out of ephemeral ports and start to love long-lived connections

items.value: Colo perimeter firewall replaced, config migrated

question: Why is every HTTPS call to ledger-core failing?
options: IPsec tunnel rekeying and dropping in-flight sessions
New firewall’s session table is full, dropping new flows
Path MTU black hole: full-size DF packets silently dropped
ledger-core’s TLS certificate is rejected by cloud clients

explanation.cause: Path MTU black hole on the new tunnel: big DF packets dropped, no ICMP back
explanation.why: The tunnel’s MTU is under 1500, and the new firewall neither clamps MSS like the old one nor returns ICMP “fragmentation needed”. Small packets pass — SYNs, ClientHellos, health checks — but the server’s certificate flight fills full-size segments that vanish, so every TLS handshake stalls.
explanation.tell: Handshakes time out rather than fail verification, plain-HTTP probes pass, and DF pings work at 1400 bytes but lose 100% at 1500 with no “Frag needed” reply.

alert.title: Synthetics: shopfront.example SERVFAIL from all public resolvers

lines.text: job backbone-capacity-audit #4471 dispatched to 212 backbone routers
ams1: dc reachability probes failing 14/14, marking site unhealthy
iad2: dc reachability probes failing 14/14, marking site unhealthy
dig www.shopfront.example @8.8.8.8: status SERVFAIL
ams1: resolver process healthy, answering on 127.0.0.1:53

items.value: ;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached

question: Why can no resolver reach shopfront.example?
options: DNSSEC signatures expired, so resolvers return SERVFAIL
Edge DNS sites withdrew their anycast prefixes from BGP
Registrar delegation changed; NS records point elsewhere
A volumetric DDoS is saturating the edge DNS links

explanation.cause: Edge DNS saw the backbone as dead and withdrew its anycast routes from BGP
explanation.why: The audit job cut every backbone link. Edge DNS hosts stop advertising their anycast prefix when they can’t reach the data centers — sensible for one sick site, fatal when every site does it at once. The servers stayed up, but no route to them existed, so resolvers had nowhere to ask.
explanation.tell: Query volume drops to zero instead of spiking, dig to the anycast IP times out instead of answering, and the looking glass has no route for the prefix at all.

alert.title: orders-api: ALB 5xx rate 0.4%, SLO burn rate 6x

items.value: nginx sidecar removed; ALB now targets Node on :3000

question: What’s producing the 502s?
options: ALB idle timeout is too short for slow order requests
Pods draining during the rollout cut off in-flight calls
Responses carry malformed headers without the sidecar
Node closes idle keep-alive sockets before the ALB does

explanation.cause: Node’s 5s keep-alive timeout is shorter than the ALB’s 60s idle timeout
explanation.why: The ALB reuses idle backend connections for up to 60s; Node’s http.Server closes them after 5s (keepAliveTimeout). When the ALB sends a request on a socket Node is closing, the target never sees it and the ALB returns 502. The old nginx sidecar kept connections for 75s.
explanation.tell: 502s are ALB-generated while target 5xx stays flat, the rate holds steady long after the deploy finished, and the only change is a target with different keep-alive defaults.

lines.text: Post "https://identity.corp.internal/v1/introspect": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid: current time 2026-04-06T12:00:31Z is after 2026-04-06T12:00:00Z
circuit breaker identity: state=open failures=100/100
Get "https://profile.corp.internal/v2/me": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid: current time 2026-04-06T12:00:31Z is after 2026-04-06T12:00:00Z

items.value: CN=*.corp.internal, issued by Corp Issuing CA 2

question: What broke internal traffic at noon?
options: Shared *.corp.internal wildcard cert passed its notAfter
Clock skew on callers makes valid certs look expired
Internal CA was rotated and callers lack the new root
A revocation push marked service certificates revoked

explanation.cause: The shared *.corp.internal wildcard certificate expired at 12:00:00
explanation.why: One wildcard cert fronted most internal services. At its notAfter every client rejected the handshake, so service-to-service traffic stopped in the same second across all regions. Expiry monitoring didn’t cover every place the cert was deployed.
explanation.tell: Every error ends “is after 2026-04-06T12:00:00Z” — one shared timestamp exactly on the hour, hitting all callers at once, with clocks within milliseconds of NTP.

alert.title: billing-export: partner upload failing on legacy batch hosts

lines.text: starting hourly partner upload (3 files) to upload.partnerhub.example
curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: certificate has expired
upload attempt 1/3 failed, retrying in 30s
depth=3 O = Digital Signature Trust Co., CN = DST Root CA X3
verify error:num=10:certificate has expired
notAfter=Sep 30 14:01:15 2021 GMT
verify return:1

question: Why do only the legacy hosts reject the partner?
options: Partner’s leaf certificate expired at 14:01 today
Partner stopped serving the R3 intermediate cert
Old OpenSSL chains to the expired DST Root CA X3
batch-01’s clock jumped past the cert’s notAfter

explanation.cause: OpenSSL 1.0.2 builds its chain to the expired DST Root CA X3, not ISRG Root X1
explanation.why: The partner serves Let’s Encrypt’s compatibility chain: leaf → R3 → ISRG Root X1 cross-signed by DST Root CA X3. OpenSSL 1.0.x follows it up to DST Root CA X3, which expired at 14:01:15 GMT, and fails instead of stopping at the trusted ISRG Root X1. OpenSSL 1.1.x finds the valid path.
explanation.tell: s_client fails at depth=3 on DST Root CA X3, not the leaf; its notAfter is six minutes before the alert, and the same upload works from hosts running OpenSSL 1.1.1.

source.title: DST Root CA X3 Expiration (September 2021) — Let’s Encrypt

alert.title: ledger.example.com: HTTPS synthetic check failing since launch

lines.text: Get "https://ledger.example.com/healthz": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate is valid for *.apps.example.com, apps.example.com, not ledger.example.com
GET https://billing.apps.example.com/healthz 200 41ms
curl: (60) SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches target host name 'ledger.example.com'

question: Why does ledger.example.com present the wrong cert?
options: ledger.example.com resolves to an old load balancer
Ingress lacks a TLS entry, so SNI gets the default cert
ledger’s new certificate is missing its intermediate
ledger’s certificate expired before the launch date

explanation.cause: ledger’s Ingress has no tls block, so ingress-nginx serves its default cert
explanation.why: ingress-nginx picks a certificate by matching SNI against hosts listed under spec.tls. ledger.example.com isn’t listed, so the controller falls back to --default-ssl-certificate, the *.apps.example.com wildcard. The ledger-tls Secret exists, but nothing references it.
explanation.tell: The cert presented is the *.apps.example.com wildcard — the controller’s default — while ledger’s own valid Secret sits unused and the Ingress has no spec.tls.

lines.text: Post "https://payments-api.mesh.internal:8443/v1/charge": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid: current time 2026-03-14T09:44:21Z is before 2026-03-14T09:49:37Z

items.value: Vault PKI, TTL 1h, renewed at ~40 min, backdated 30s
Those 2 run canary AMI v57; the rest run v56

question: Why do these bursts keep recurring?
options: Vault agent renews too late, so certs lapse before swap
Two nodes kept a stale CA bundle from before a CA rotation
payments-api serves the old cert until its pods restart
Clocks on two nodes lag, so fresh certs aren’t valid yet

explanation.cause: Clocks on two canary-AMI nodes run ~6 min slow; fresh certs look not-yet-valid
explanation.why: Vault backdates notBefore by only 30s. After each renewal, a node whose clock lags ~6 min sees a certificate from its future and rejects it until its own clock passes notBefore — a burst every ~40 min. The canary AMI shipped without a working time sync client.
explanation.tell: The error says “is before” (not yet valid), not “is after”; only two nodes fail; and their log timestamps sit ~6 min behind the 09:50 renewal they’re rejecting.

question: Which line explains why lookups still fail after the record exists?

explanation.cause: An NXDOMAIN cached before the record existed outlived the cutover
explanation.why: A lookup at 03:00:12 hit dns-cache 40s before Terraform finished creating the record. Route 53 answered NXDOMAIN with its SOA, and the cache kept it for min(SOA TTL, SOA minimum) = 900s. Every lookup until ~03:15 gets the cached “no such host”, though the record exists.
explanation.tell: The NXDOMAIN at 03:00:12 lands between “Creating...” and “Creation complete”, and dns-cache’s TTL of 529 at 03:06:23 counts down from exactly that moment.
